title: Romancing the Stone
tagline: Lost in the jungle, found a good sancocho.
about: A shy romance novelist heads to Colombia to rescue her sister and lands in a real adventure.
cue: Serve the snacks when Joan finishes her latest novel at her New York flat.

    StartersColombian arepas con quesoGriddled white corn cakes with cheese and a fried tomato and onion hogaoHow to make it300g pre-cooked white cornmeal500ml warm water1 tsp salt40g butter200g mozzarella3 tomatoes4 spring onions2 tbsp oilMix the cornmeal, warm water and salt into a soft dough and rest.Shape 8 patties about 1.5cm thick.Cook in a buttered pan over medium heat until golden on both sides.Fry diced tomatoes and sliced spring onions in oil to make the hogao.Split the arepas and stuff with sliced mozzarella and a knob of butter.Serve with the hogao.Cartagena empanadasFried beef and potato empanadas with a green coriander sauceHow to make it300g beef mince1 potato, diced1 tsp ground cumin250g arepa flour350ml warm water1 bunch coriander1 green chilli1 lime1 L vegetable oil, for fryingsalt, to tasteFry the mince with the potato and cumin until cooked through.Cool the filling completely.Mix the arepa flour with warm water and salt to a dough.Flatten balls of dough, fill, fold and crimp the edges.Fry at 180°C until crisp and golden.Blitz coriander, chilli, lime and a little oil for the sauce.MainsColombian sancochoChicken soup with corn, potatoes, cassava and green plantainHow to make it1kg chicken thighs2.5 L water1 brown onion2 cloves of garlic3 corn cobs500g potatoes400g cassava1 green plantain1 bunch coriander300g long grain rice2 avocadosPeel and chop the onion, garlic, potatoes, cassava and plantain, and cut the corn into chunks.Simmer the chicken in water with the onion and garlic.Add the corn, potatoes, cassava and plantain and simmer until thick.Cook the rice while the soup simmers.Finish with coriander and serve with rice and sliced avocado.Cartagena snapper with coconut riceThe run to Cartagena for the final showdownHow to make itAs written, serves 4Whole snapper scored and rubbed with lime, garlic and chilli, grilled crisp, served with Caribbean coconut rice, fried green plantain and a tomato and onion salsa.Score 2 whole 600g snapper and rub with 3 crushed garlic cloves, a chopped chilli, lime juice, oil and salt.Cook 300g rice in 400ml coconut milk and 200ml water, covered, for 15 minutes.Slice a green plantain, fry at 180°C until golden, smash flat and fry again.Grill the fish over high heat for 8 minutes a side.Serve with the rice, plantain and a salsa of diced tomato, red onion and lime.SweetsEl Corazón emerald jellyFresh lime jelly set in a mould, with chilled coconut cream and mintHow to make it6 gelatine leaves300ml water150g caster sugar250ml fresh lime juice (about 10 limes)200ml coconut cream1 small bunch mintSoak the gelatine leaves in cold water.Heat the water with the sugar until dissolved.Squeeze the gelatine and stir it in, then add the lime juice.Pour into a mould.Set in the fridge.Turn out and serve with chilled coconut cream and mint.DrinksJoan Wilder's iced coffee with panela creamStrong cinnamon panela coffee over ice under lightly whipped creamHow to make it60g ground Colombian coffee1 L hot water100g panela or dark brown sugar1 cinnamon stick150ml thickened creamground cinnamon, to dust1 bag iceBrew the coffee strong with the hot water.While hot, stir in most of the panela and the cinnamon stick.Cool for 30 minutes and remove the cinnamon stick.Lightly whip the cream with a spoonful of the panela until just thick.Fill four glasses with ice, pour in the coffee, float the cream on top and dust with cinnamon.
